newsitem.title: USA: Maryland center would need $200 mln in bonds.
newsitem.headline: Maryland center would need $200 mln in bonds.

text.p: The developer of the proposed $585 million American Dream entertainment center submitted a financing plan for the Montgomery County, Md., project that calls for state issuance of roughly $200 million in revenue bonds, a spokesman for the developer said Tuesday.

Charles Maier, a spokesman for the project developer Triple Five Group of Edmonton, Alberta, said in a telephone interview that between 75 and 85 percent of the total project cost would be financed "from the project's own revenues."

"That's a combination of two things," he said. One is direct, private capital investments. The other is "reinvestment of a portion of...public revenues generated by the project to pay off...bonds," Maier said.
He said Triple Five thinks about $200 million in revenue bonds are needed.

State or local government would pay the rest of the 15 to 25 percent of total project costs for infrastructure like road improvements, public transportation, mass transit links like pedestrian walkways, land purchases, and utility extensions and relocations, Maier said.
The proposal's reliance on revenue bonds for about one-third of its financing is likely to run into hot water with key local officials.

"I've told them I will not do county revenue bonds. (And) I can't support state revenue bonds," Douglas Duncan, Montgomery County executive said in a telephone interview after receiving Triple Five's project plan late Monday.
"If you go down to (the state capital in) Annapolis and ask them for money, the first thing they ask you is, 'Why isn't the county doing revenue bonds?' " Duncan said.
He continued, "We say it's too risky. Then they look at you and say, 'Why isn't it too risky for us then?' "
Duncan said he expects to make a decision in two weeks. "If it doesn't work, we'll thank them and move on to something else," said Duncan.

The proposed 28-acre project is designed to revitalize downtown Silver Spring, Md., a suburb of Washington, D.C. It would have an amusement park, ice skating rink, wave pool, restaurants, theaters and stores and other attractions.
Triple Five said in a one-page statement today that the project will be a model for "urban community economic development" for the 21st century.

"The American Dream Town Center project will provide returns...from the day it opens," said Triple Five, whose 10-year-old Mall of American near Minneapolis generates roughly $1 billion in economic activity annually.
"Millions of dollars of property taxes will be paid directly by the developer for land on which almost nothing is being paid today," the group said.

"Thousands of new jobs will be created and additional tax revenues to help support schools, libraries, and other public services will be provided primarily by tourists and other new visitors to the area," the group said.
Maier said the project would not be an "enclosed monolithic mall. It all opens to the street as well as the interior."
